decisions.rationale: ICoinLedger declares MergeFrom and CoinProvenanceStore implements it as a direct expression-bodied call to _wal.Merge(ops).
MergeFrom has no statements other than _wal.Merge(ops); no validation, type check, conservation check, witness verification, or CommutativeOpProcessor call is present.
Append throws on CoinOpType.Spend, AppendCommittedSpend is the gated spend path, but MergeFrom writes to the same WAL through _wal.Merge without that guard.

The repo contains a corpus copy of GLPNET PgliteOpWal; its Merge loops through Append, and Append calls InsertOp with documented ON CONFLICT/dot idempotence. The behavior is verifiable in this repo, even if the csproj references an external checkout.
MergeFrom only merges into the WAL and does not call Project. The anti-entropy test observes merged balances only by constructing fresh CommutativeOpProcessor instances over the stores.

The constructor comment explicitly labels the peer-merge validation gap as CROSS-HOST FOLLOW-UP/OE-4 and says rehydration projects WAL ops without admission checks or witness-cert verification; MergeFrom and rehydration must re-validate later.
The constructor rehydrates by iterating ledger.OpsIn(CoinBoxes.Ledger) and calling Project(envelope) directly; there is no Validate call in that replay loop.

Validate is projection-order dependent: split/merge/charge/aging reject unseen mints/leaves, and deps passed to Op.Create are not used by Validate. Non-causal peer deltas could reject otherwise valid dependent ops.
Replay calls Validate before Project, while Validate maps SpendBody to RejectedMalformed. The nearby follow-up comment says Replay must accept committed SpendBody so recovery paths agree.
ValidateMint checks value, provider, duplicate mint id, funding sum, and pool bound only. In Ledger, witness-cert verification is on the spend gate path, not in mint admission.

PoolAudit adds mint.FundingFreshUCoin to fresh, computes circulating from replay, and checks circulating + pool == fresh. A fresh-funded forged mint increases both fresh and circulating; only poolOut > poolIn and DAG conservation are separately checked.
Project(MintBody) subtracts FundingPoolUCoin but clamps to zero when it exceeds _poolCredits, with the comment saying the pool audit convicts forged overdraws instead of crashing.
Repo-scope grep under Olamnit.Coin.Tests/Ledger finds only two MergeFrom calls, both in AntiEntropy_ConvergesTwoReplicas, which exchanges two valid Mint ops and then rehydrates projections.

EndorseAsync enforces independence by string.Equals(endorserKeyId, claim.WalletId). The injected _bindings registry is used in derive/resolve/readmit paths, not in EndorseAsync, despite the class docs saying resolution to claimant binding is rejected.

EndorserKey is derived from HostIdentity with a domain prefix, but wallet_id is an arbitrary string accepted by ActorWalletBindingRegistry.BindAsync/admin surface. The code does not make equality structurally impossible.

IndependentVerifier chooses an ICorroborationSource by SourceKind. Both shipped sources take an injected liveNativeIds delegate and return evidence only from live.Contains(signal.SourceNativeId); neither verifies a signature.

The seeded reward mapping list contains exactly three SeedMapping rows: stage-complete-co, kernel-work-trace, and kernel-work-typed. Repo-scope grep in rewards shows no relay-hop/per-hop policy class.

Reward policy is data-driven by SourceKind/capture_method: IndependentVerifier does a source dictionary lookup, MatchAsync rereads active mappings per call, and MappingSeed is an init-settable option. No ledger engine type change is implied by a new reward class.

The absence of a signature-verifying ICorroborationSource is checkable and true, but whether a hypothetical next-hop-signed ACK would satisfy the contract is a design judgement not settled by current repo code.
TryFloorSplit refuses k greater than the ucoin value, so 1 ucoin cannot split into 2+. ValidateMerge rejects parents from different mint DAGs, and RewardMinter derives one mint id from each claim id.
MicroCoin documents 1 coin = 1,000,000 ucoin and UCoinPerCoin is 1,000,000. The seeded CO stage-completion reward is 1,000,000 ucoin, i.e. one whole coin.

The processor keeps unbounded dictionaries for DAGs and leaf indexes. Project(MintBody) creates a new CoinDag/root leaf per new mint. The constructor and PoolAudit replay all WAL ledger ops through a fresh processor.
FindLiveLeavesOf scans _leafToMint with LINQ Where and orders the result. It is called by ValidateAging and Project(AgingBody), so each aging op scans the current leaf dictionary.
Admit locks on the single _lock object and holds it while generating the dot, validating, appending to the WAL, and projecting. All local commutative mint admissions share this lock.

ProcessAsync sequentially performs admission, claim derivation, parked resolution, auto endorsement, and mint. The called methods issue the SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE queries named in the claim; the 20-25 count is a trace-based estimate, not a timing measurement.

RewardSchema itself has no guard and calls conn.InitializeAsync each time, but the repo includes IPgliteConnection/PgliteInterop and pglite-edge.js. initEdge memoizes _dbPromise and only openDb executes DDL on first initialization, so memoization is verifiable.

Olamnit.Coin.Rewards.csproj has a single ProjectReference to Olamnit.Coin. Olamnit.Coin.csproj is what references Olamnit.Shared, and the rewards using of Olamnit.Shared.Content.Interop is therefore transitive.

Olamnit.Coin.csproj documents an external GLPNET checkout pinned by commit, defaults GlpnetRoot to D:/bstdev/glp/GLPNET, and ProjectReferences $(GlpnetRoot)/csharp/glp_crdtmsg/GlpCrdtMsg.csproj. No package reference replaces it.

AutoClaimExpiry defaults to 24h and the auto seed rows use 24h windows. ExpirySweep closes awaiting claims with expires_at before now as expired_unendorsed, and the ingestion loop defaults the sweep interval to 15 minutes.

reward_signal/claim/endorsement/mint are PGlite tables in RewardSchema. RewardMinter writes reward_mint through _conn, while coin anti-entropy DeltaFor/MergeFrom only moves WAL Ops; the reward evidence tables are not appended to the coin WAL by this pipeline.

The repo confirms Olamnit.Coin.Rewards.Tests exists with 16 files, including Soaks and Integration, but the builder's claim about what was outside their slice or what they personally assessed is not resolvable from repo contents alone.
